Hazy skies: Boys sitting on a wooden jetty along the Kahayan River as haze from wildfires shrouds the area in Palangka Raya, Central Kalimantan province, in this file photo. — Reuters 
 President Pra­bowo Subi­an­to has apologised to Malaysia and Singapore over a toxic haze caused by rampant wildfires in his country that polluted the skies of Indonesia’s neighbours.
 The months-long blazes on Bor­neo, Sumatra and Papua razed vast tracts of land and produced air pollution that sickened hundreds of thousands at home and drifted across borders to Malaysia and Singapore.
 Prabowo told a summit of the Association of South-East Asian Nations (Asean) in Manila on Sun­day that the transboundary haze was “not our fault” and insisted that “we have done our best”.
 However, “on behalf of the Indonesian government, Indone­sian people, we apologise if we have created suffering for the people of Singapore and Malay­sia”, he told leaders of Asean mem­ber states, according to a video of the plenary session released by the presidential secretariat.
 Wildfires have burned through some 2.88 million hectares so far in 2026, according to the Nusan­tara Atlas deforestation monitor, an area 18 times the size of London.
 Indonesia experiences fires every dry season, but this year’s blazes have been particularly severe.
 Researchers said last week that a strong El Nino weather phenomenon, climate change, deforestation and peatland drainage for mining and plantations have supercharged this year’s Indonesian fire season.
 Prabowo said Indonesian autho­rities had revoked 17 land concessions from corporations in connection with the blazes and 26 others were under investigation.
 He said Indonesia had deployed 71,000 people to tackle the blazes, noting the country lost 16 firefighters and two helicopters in firefighting missions. — AFP
